title: Quadrant dependence, reflected copula measures and exchangeable ranks
shortTitle: Quadrant dependence and PMI part ways near independence
oneLine: All four Fuchs–Tschimpke implications fail, and exact limits for exchangeable ranks
abstract: Fuchs and Tschimpke introduced the positive measure inducing (PMI) property of a bivariate copula, which orders a family of concordance measures and yields the population inequality 3γ ≥ 2ρ between Gini's gamma and Spearman's rho. They conjectured that for Archimedean copulas PMI is equivalent to positive quadrant dependence (PQD), and NMI to NQD; Graham refuted PQD ⇒ PMI. This candidate shows that all four implications fail arbitrarily close to independence, with real-analytic Archimedean generators, positive densities and explicit parameters, in every finite dimension. Ordered comparisons of concordance measures detect exactly the symmetrised reflected measure, and no finite family of comparisons characterises PMI. Shared-frailty copulas with two frailty values are always PMI, while three values (rates 1, 2 and 200) can fail it, even with a density totally positive of every order. For a pair of ranks that extends to n exchangeable ranks, the exact range of 3γ − 2sρ is determined for every slope −n/2 ≤ s ≤ 1; for n = 3, 3γ − 2ρ ≥ −23/54 and γ ≥ −4/9. The same construction gives the exact smallest common pairwise generalised Gini's gamma in every dimension, a question of Koike and Hofert. Limits: the counterexamples are tiny effects with no claim about test power; all statements are about populations; the full attainable sets remain open. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

evidence: A 14-page paper with a context-first introduction, written proofs of every result, limits, open problems and an AI-use statement. Two Python programs accompany it: verify.py checks every exact constant in exact rational arithmetic (effect-size slopes, the three-rate frailty certificate, the closed forms of d_n(s), −23/54, −4/9, attainment in 56 cases), and check_grid.py solves 18 finite-grid linear programs that agree with the exchangeability theorem. A clean replay in Python's optimised mode reproduced both recorded outputs; a changed constant makes verify.py fail; Linux CI reruns both.

keyResults: Theorem 3.1 (proof): PMI ⇒ PQD, NMI ⇒ NQD, NQD ⇒ NMI and PQD ⇒ PMI all fail for real-analytic Archimedean copulas arbitrarily close to independence, with explicit ranges 0 < |ε| ≤ 10⁻³ and 0 < |ε| ≤ 10⁻⁸, in every finite dimension; in the PQD example 3γ − 2ρ < 0.
Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.2 (proof): concordance comparisons detect exactly the symmetrised reflected measure; no finite family of comparisons characterises PMI.
Proposition 5.1 and Corollary 5.2 (proof): two frailty values always give PMI; three (rates 1, 2 and 200) can fail it, even with a density totally positive of every order.

Theorem 6.1 and Corollary 6.2 (proof): for n exchangeable ranks and −n/2 ≤ s ≤ 1, 3γ − 2sρ ranges exactly over [d_n(s), 3 − 2s]; d_n(s) = −(3 − 2s)/(n − 1) for even n; for n = 3, 3γ − 2ρ ≥ −23/54 and γ ≥ −4/9.

Theorem 7.1 (proof): the exact smallest common pairwise generalised Gini's gamma in every dimension; for n = 3 ordinary Gini's gamma it is −4/9 (Koike–Hofert Gaussian example about −0.379; correlation bound −1/2).

Credit and limits: Fuchs–Tschimpke (definition, theorem, conjecture), Graham (first counterexample), Ansari–Rockel–Steinmaßl, Koike–Hofert, Fuchs (2024) and Müller–Scarsini supply tools. The counterexamples are tiny effects; all statements are about populations; the full attainable sets remain open.
